findings.title: Final-inventory cache suppresses durable later refusal
counterexamples: save(release-decision.json) fails after one successful final inventory: FD9 remains held but no durable cause/refusal
close(9) raises with unknown outcome: final snapshot still reports pre-close STILL_HELD; no new durable uncertainty record
save(owner-result.json) fails after confirmed release: no durable refusal; pre-release snapshot remains the only final-bus evidence
findings.cause: The actual outer exception handler only sets __parent_error. persist_final_bus_inventory returns cached ref before the only parent-refusal save block can observe that error.
findings.fix_scope: Preserve exactly one post-cleanup bus snapshot. Persist a separate once-only refusal/outcome record after the original failure even when the final snapshot already exists, referencing that snapshot and distinguishing attempted/unconfirmed FD9 close from confirmed release. Do not retry close/send/snapshot or infer cessation. Evidence-write failure stays explicit and causal error retained.

findings.title: Publisher and loader traversal retry ambiguous close and lose another owned FD
counterexamples: safe_parent: first close of old ancestor FD51 succeeds then raises; outer except closes51 again, masks first error with KeyError in finite FD model, leaves newly opened FD52 unclosed
capture_source: wrong hash plus source close exception skips held parent close; original wrong-hash cause remains only exception context; no return record
exact root loader capture reproduces duplicate ancestor close and leaked next FD
findings.cause: Ownership changes only after old close returns, and sequential close operations in finally are not individually protected.
findings.fix_scope: Transfer/track each owned descriptor before fallible close, mark one close attempt per descriptor, and attempt every remaining owned close independently of previous cleanup errors while retaining causal failure and explicit cleanup uncertainty. Apply to minimal publisher and exact loader; regenerate owner literal/wrapper from repaired bytes. No retry, fallback publisher or new framework.

Exact owner-command and wrapper embed the selected loader. Wrapper was parsed only and inherits F2; never executed.
